clue.text: Rock and roll's first grand hit, with Joe Strummer

indicators.note: to rock is to shake or jolt, so these letters are shaken into a new order
first says only the opening letter of roll's is used

explanation.surface: A tribute to the Clash frontman Joe Strummer scoring a big rock and roll hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre but is the anagram signal; 'Strummer' looks like part of Joe Strummer's name but is the definition. The fodder is AND, R, GRAND, HIT and JOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Django Reinhardt was a celebrated Belgian-born jazz guitarist, and a guitarist is someone who strums.

clue.text: Retailer's name in credit

indicators.note: in says the word for name sits inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
a handle is slang for a name, as with an online username

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's name appearing in the credits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retailer's' is the definition plus the link 's (is).
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in supplies such as candles or ship's provisions, so a kind of retailer.

clue.text: Make unclear, novel advert cut short

indicators.note: cut short says the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text on the cover of a novel

explanation.surface: An advert for a novel trimmed so much it becomes confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last B of BLURB.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to smudge it so its outline can no longer be seen clearly.

clue.text: New boy dips into illicit money, a career-ending moment

indicators.note: dips into says the next pieces go inside the word for illicit money

parts.note: swag is stolen goods or loot
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A young lad dabbling in dirty money, ruining his career.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a final performance before retirement, from the myth of the dying swan singing.

clue.text: Horridly vacuous cops running around in film

indicators.note: running around suggests things moving about chaotically, so these letters are scrambled
vacuous means emptied, so only the outer letters of Horridly remain

explanation.surface: Police officers dashing about in a dreadfully empty-headed way in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horridly vacuous' reads as a description of the cops, but 'vacuous' empties the word to its outer letters, which join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is the 1960 Alfred Hitchcock horror movie set at the Bates Motel.

clue.text: Spooner's to rent clothing for terrier?

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped, after the reverend famed for this slip

parts.note: to hire is to rent
wear means clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: Asking whether hired clothes might suit a terrier.
explanation.walkthrough: HIRE WEAR with initial sounds swapped gives WIRE HAIR; the swap is by sound, as WEAR becomes HAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A wirehair is a terrier breed with a rough wiry coat, such as the wire fox terrier.

clue.text: Arm broken by fellow when climbing Italian building

indicators.note: broken by says the word for arm is split open by what follows

parts.note: an Uzi is a submachine gun, so a firearm

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing says the word for when is read from bottom to top

parts.note: if can mean when, as in 'if you see her, wave'

explanation.surface: An arm injured by a man scaling an Italian structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a limb but means a weapon; 'climbing' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi in Florence is a famous art gallery housed in a Renaissance palazzo.

clue.text: Labour's beast trashed May: "An abhorrent leader of idiots"

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so these letters are smashed up and reassembled
leader of says only the opening letter of idiots is taken

explanation.surface: A Labour politician insulting Theresa May as the leader of fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' suggests the Labour Party but means a Labour of Hercules. 'trashed' scrambles MAY, AN, ABHORRENT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Capturing the Erymanthian boar was the fourth of the twelve Labours of Hercules.

clue.text: Detective's behind convenience store

indicators.note: behind places the detective after the word for convenience

parts.note: a convenience is a public toilet, slangily a john
Lewis is the TV police detective, sidekick of Inspector Morse; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A detective lurking behind a corner shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convenience store' reads as one phrase, but 'store' alone is the definition; a convenience is a British public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lewis is a well-known British department store chain.

clue.text: Reason reporter's dressed to anger animal activists

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the words are said out loud to suggest another spelling

parts.note: wearing a fur coat, which would upset animal rights campaigners

explanation.surface: A journalist explaining they wore something to annoy animal-rights protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to deduce or conclude from evidence, which is what inferring means.

clue.text: Zidane's refusal to get club's kind of shirt?

parts.note: Zinedine Zidane is French, and non is French for no
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A French footballer turning down a club's shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a football club, given Zidane, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-iron shirt is made of fabric that needs no pressing after washing.

clue.text: Extremely abrasive music could be metal

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be rearranged into something else
extremely points to the two extreme letters of abrasive

explanation.surface: Very harsh music might count as heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal' looks like the music genre but is the definition. 'Extremely' gives AE, which 'could be' mixes with MUSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesium is a soft alkali metal, element 55, used in atomic clocks.

clue.text: Hearts broken from wails in parliament?

indicators.note: broken from says the card-suit letter is snapped off the word for wails

parts.note: howls are long loud cries, like wails
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: Broken-hearted wailing heard in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parliament' suggests Westminster but is the collective noun for these birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is the collective noun for a group of these nocturnal birds of prey.

clue.text: I'm amazed by old people's investment

indicators.note: by places the pieces side by side

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
a nation is a people; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Astonishment at a pensioner's investment portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' suggests money but here means formally investing someone with office.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment can mean the ceremony of installing someone in office, as when a monarch is crowned.

clue.text: East Londoner's trial, after hiding queen's jewellery

indicators.note: hiding says the next letter is concealed within the word before

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so a hearing (a trial) becomes 'earing
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A Cockney stands trial for hiding the Queen's jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: An East Londoner is a Cockney, whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is a piece of jewellery worn on the ear lobe.

clue.text: I'm giving up, overwhelmed by current state of US injustice

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the phrase is swallowed up by the letters around it

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York state
'I quit' is what someone says when giving up

explanation.surface: Someone resigning in despair at the unfair condition of America.
explanation.definitionFit: An iniquity is a grossly unfair or wicked act, a gross wrong.

clue.text: Slight injury is no handicap

definitions.meaning: a minor graze or nick on the skin
in golf a ... player has a handicap of zero

explanation.surface: A minor wound is no obstacle to carrying on.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape on the skin is a minor wound; in golf a player off zero handicap is called this.

clue.text: Function assumed by Poles or Greeks

indicators.note: assumed by says the function is taken in by the word for poles

parts.note: spars are poles, as used for masts on ships
tan, short for tangent, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A role taken on by either Poles or Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests PART and 'Poles' the letters N and S, a dead end; the function is trigonometric and the poles are ship's masts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartans were citizens of Sparta, a powerful city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Experimental equipment fixed up underground — about time!

indicators.note: about says the earlier pieces sit around the letter for time
in a down clue up says the word for fixed is read upwards

parts.note: set means fixed, as in a set price
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Kit for the London Underground finally repaired, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about time!' reads as an exclamation of relief, but 'about' places the earlier letters around the one for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is a glass tube used to hold samples in laboratory experiments.

clue.text: Thatcherite maybe stirring up a rebellion

indicators.note: stirring up suggests agitating something, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A Thatcher supporter perhaps fomenting revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher championed free-market economics, so her followers are an example of free-market believers.

clue.text: Green welcoming tax rises in fixed interval

indicators.note: in a down clue rises says the whole is read from bottom to top
welcoming says the tax is taken in by the word for green

parts.note: eco is a prefix meaning green or environmental
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An environmentalist accepting tax increases at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses the whole combination, EVATCO, not just the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this is the interval of eight notes between one pitch and the next of the same name.

clue.text: Four card players wrapping party gifts

indicators.note: wrapping says the four players surround the word for party

parts.note: the four bridge players are named by compass points: E, N, W and S
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Bridge players wrapping up presents for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gifts' looks like a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone is to give them money or a quality, as in to bestow upon them.

clue.text: Spies in Jerusalem uncovered bones

indicators.note: uncovered says the covering letters at each end are stripped off

parts.note: Mossad is Israel's intelligence service

explanation.surface: Secret agents in Jerusalem dig up skeletal remains.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for a bone.

clue.text: Shock: divas to undress, partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Opera stars stripping off would be shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to amaze or stun them greatly.

clue.text: Machine's secure, stopping end revolving

indicators.note: stopping says the word for secure plugs a gap in the other word
revolving says the word for end is turned round

parts.note: a butt is an end, as of a cigarette
to win is to secure, as in win a contract

explanation.surface: A device that is safe, preventing a part from spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns the word for end round to TTUB before 'stopping' plugs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is an old-style washing machine with separate wash and spin drums.

clue.text: How month starts to turn cold

indicators.note: to turn says the letters are turned around

parts.note: Dec 1, written DEC I, is how the last month begins

explanation.surface: Asking how a month begins to grow chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: The month in question is December, its first day written Dec 1 with the 1 as a Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means chilled or frozen, so very cold.

clue.text: Cover musical composition with verse included

indicators.note: included says the letter for verse is placed inside

parts.note: a duet is a piece of music for two performers

explanation.surface: Covering a song with an extra verse added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song, but means a bed covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet is a quilted bedcover filled with down or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Speculate British artist is a fashioner of busts

parts.note: to wonder is to speculate or ponder
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Pondering whether a British artist is a sculptor of busts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busts' suggests sculpture, but means bosoms.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a push-up bra brand that shapes and lifts the wearer's bosom.
